title: Build a deterministic ETL pipeline and replicate it on holdout plus a generated probe
goal: A three-stage data-reproducibility campaign. Stage 1: implement a CSV metrics pipeline whose output byte-matches the sealed dev golden under an exact serialization spec. Stage 2: prove determinism - the grader runs the pipeline twice and requires byte-identical output. Stage 3: replicate on the sealed holdout dataset AND on a probe dataset the grader generates fresh at grading time from a sealed seed, compared against its own internal reference computation - so hard-coding the shipped goldens cannot pass. The plan, sha256 stage-marker chain, and run journal are graded with final state as one campaign_score.
resources: pypi pytest==8.3.4 (installed by the sealed grader inside the container)
assets/gc-412/SPEC.md (normative metric + serialization spec, artifact contract)
assets/gc-412/grade.py + assets/gc-412/config.json (sealed campaign grader with probe generator)
process_expectations: A frozen plan decomposes the metric spec (typing rule, padding rule, rounding, serialization) before any pipeline code, pinned by the marker chain.
runs.log journals each self-verification (dev diff, double-run diff, holdout diff) as JSON lines with honest pass/fail outcomes.
Byte-level mismatches are diagnosed by identity (which column, which field) rather than regenerated blindly - visible as multiple journaled attempts when stage 1 was RED.
Determinism is verified, not assumed: the grader executes the pipeline twice and compares bytes.
Generalization is verified on unseen data: the grader-generated probe dataset must match the grader's reference computation exactly.

assets_visibility.note: sealed files live in the maintainers' private sealed pack; public repo keeps <name>.sha256 commitments. Restore with tools/restore_sealed.py before grading these cards.
